paper_title: Can We Edit LLMs for Long-Tail Biomedical Knowledge
caption: : The performance on BioGPT.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC %) of different methods for editing a large language model (BioGPT) as a function of the co-occurrence number, which is displayed on a logarithmic scale ranging from 1 to 10^3 (i.e., 1 to 1000). The y-axis represents accuracy in percentage, ranging from 30% to 55%, with major gridlines at 5% intervals. Six methods are compared: Base (black solid line with circular markers), FT (blue solid line with downward-pointing triangle markers), IKE (red solid line with upward-pointing triangle markers), MEND (brown solid line with diamond markers), MEMIT (purple solid line with circular markers), and ROME (green solid line with square markers). All lines show an increasing trend in accuracy as co-occurrence number increases. The Base method remains the lowest, starting at approximately 30% and ending near 33%. FT starts at about 33% and ends near 37%. IKE starts at around 33% and reaches approximately 40%. MEND begins at about 37% and plateaus near 45%. MEMIT starts at approximately 37% and ends near 46%. ROME shows the highest performance, starting at about 43% and rising to nearly 56% at the highest co-occurrence number.
